analysis: Cholecystokinin (CCK) is a well-studied gastrointestinal hormone with specific roles in the digestive system. It is primarily known for causing the contraction of the gallbladder, which aids in the release of bile into the small intestine. Additionally, CCK stimulates the secretion of pancreatic juice that is rich in digestive enzymes, facilitating the breakdown of fats, proteins, and carbohydrates. These actions are well-documented and supported by medical consensus. However, the role of CCK in the secretion of enterokinase, an enzyme involved in protein digestion, is not clearly established or supported by strong evidence. Therefore, while options (opa) and (opb) are correct, option (opc) lacks sufficient evidence. Consequently, option (opd) which includes all the listed actions, is incorrect due to the inclusion of the unsupported action (opc). Based on this analysis, the most accurate answer, supported by medical consensus, is to select the options that are well-supported.
